key_insight: The paper proposes a heterogeneity-aware diffusion Schrodinger bridge that uses region context and PET guidance to improve whole-body MRI translation across anatomically diverse areas and lesions.
clinical_relevance: This could help shorten PET-MR workflows by generating higher-quality MRI from limited inputs, especially in challenging whole-body and lesion-rich regions.
method: Uses a diffusion Schrodinger bridge to model stochastic transport between source and target MRI distributions.
Adds vision-language model region embeddings for anatomy-specific translation across the whole body.
Injects PET-derived lesion and metabolic priors during both forward noise modulation and reverse attention-guided denoising.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports improved translation quality across different body regions and better lesion-area performance under PET guidance, based on experimental evaluation.
watch_item: Performance may depend on reliable PET availability and region/lesion priors, which could limit deployment when multimodal inputs are incomplete or noisy.
paper_title: Heterogeneity-Adaptive Diffusion Schrodinger Bridge for PET-Guided Whole-Body MRI Translation
